problem_en: We were able to open the housing of a defective plug power supply relatively non-destructive and discover a defective thermal protection. Unfortunately, when releasing this also a winding wire of the transformer ripped off, which unfortunately was no longer to be repaired.

problem: Er wollte keine CDs mehr abspielen. Leider scheiterten alle Reinigungs- und Reparaturversuche, sodass er leider auch zukünftig keine dünnen Scheiben mehr drehen wird.
problem_en: He didn't want to play any more CDs. Unfortunately, all cleaning and repair attempts failed, so that he will not turn any thin discs in the future.

problem: Die Erkennung des gefüllten Wassertanks funktionierte an einer Kaffeepad-Maschine nicht mehr zuverlässig. Ein Fehler war nicht zu finden. Vermutlich verträgt sich das Paar aus Magnet und Magnetschalter nicht mehr so gut.
problem_en: The detection of the filled water tank was no longer reliable on a coffee pad machine. It was impossible to find an error. Probably the pair of magnet and magnetic switch can no longer cope so well.

problem: Ihre Kraft hatte deutlich nachgelassen; Möhren wurden nicht mehr richtig gehäckselt wie früher. Während des Zerlegens mutmaßten wir, dass die Rutschkupplung zwischen Motorwelle und Mitnehmer der Häckselscheiben zu schnell nachgab. Nach weiterem Zerlegen des Antriebs mussten wir feststellen, dass die vermeintliche Rutschkupplung eigentlich eine feste Verbindung beider Teile sein sollte, die der Motor überdreht hatte und nun durchrutschte. Beim nächsten Mal werden wir diese feste Verbindung mit Zwei-Komponenten-Kleber wieder herstellen.
problem_en: Their power had decreased significantly; carrots were no longer hogged properly as before. During the disassembly we assumed that the slip clutch between the motor shaft and the co-driver gave way too quickly. After further disassembly of the drive, we had to find out that the supposed slip clutch should actually be a fixed connection of both parts, which the engine had overturned and now slipped through. Next time we will establish this fixed connection with two-component glue again.

problem: Er war heruntergefallen und dabei auf der Netzkabelbuchse geladet, die im Gehäuse verschwand. Diese konnten wir nach dem Öffnen des Gerätes wieder anbringen. Nun musiziert er wieder fröhlich.
problem_en: He had fallen down and loaded it on the mains cable socket, which disappeared in the housing. We were able to put it back on after opening the device. Now he plays again cheerfully.

problem: Sie hatte die komische Eigenart entwickelt, beim Öffnen der Tür einen Kurzschluss auszulösen, wobei die Sicherung durchbrannte. Ansonsten funktionierte sie tadellos. Beim Öffnen des Gerätes waren wir angenehm überrascht, einen Schaltplan vorzufinden - sehr gut! Anhand dessen konnte der Defekt schnell gefunden werden: einer der vier (!) Türschalter klemmte und verursachte den Kurzschluss. Den Schalter haben wir wieder gangbar gemacht und die Mikrowelle war wieder ohne Macke.
problem_en: She had developed the funny way of triggering a short circuit when opening the door, whereby the fuse burned through. Otherwise, it worked perfectly. When opening the device we were pleasantly surprised to find a schematic - very good! On the basis of this the defect could be found quickly: one of the four (!) door switches clamped and caused the short circuit. We made the switch again manageable and the microwave was again without Macke.

problem_en: The power switch was broken, a piece was broken. Unfortunately, nothing could be done, as it was a very special switch and not to be repaired.

problem: Das elektronisches Innenleben einer niedliche Puppe tat nichts mehr. Sie konnte nicht mehr schreien, sich bewegen und die Augen zu klappen. Genervte Eltern wären froh darüber ;-), aber wir versuchten es zu reparieren. Leider war die gesamte Elektronik im Puppenkopf untergebracht, den wir nicht öffnen konnten ohne einen Schaden zu riskieren. Das wollten wir dem niedlichen kleinen Ding nicht antun.
problem_en: The electronic interior of a cute doll didn't do anything anymore. She couldn't scream anymore, move and open her eyes. Irritated parents would be happy about it ;-), but we tried to fix it. Unfortunately, all the electronics were in the doll's head, which we couldn't open without risking damage. We didn't want to do that to the cute little thing.

problem: Bei dem Notebook-Netzteil konnte ein Wackelkontakt entdeckt werden, aber weitere Defekte - kaputte Sicherung und verschmorte Leiterbahn - wiesen auf irreparable Defekte hin.
problem_en: With the notebook power supply a wobble contact could be discovered, but further defects - broken fuse and blurred conductor track - pointed to irreparable defects.

problem: Funktionierte nicht mehr. Wir konnte als Ursache abgenutzte Kohlebürsten feststellen. Der unterschiedliche Abnutzungsgrad lässt wieder einmal geplante Obsoleszenz vermuten.
problem_en: We were able to identify worn carbon brushes as the cause. The different degree of wear makes us suspect once again planned obsolescence.

problem: Heizlüfter funktionierte einfach zu gut - er lief auch noch weiter, wenn er umgefallen war, was eigentlich ein Kontakt verhindern sollte. Dieser konnte repariert werden und nun geht der Lüfter aus, wenn er nicht dasteht, wie er soll.
problem_en: Heating fan worked just too well - it went even further when it had fallen, which was supposed to prevent contact. It could be repaired and now the fan runs out if it doesn't stand there as it should.

problem: Die Daten von einem alten Telefon sollten auf ein neues übertragen werden. Das Datenkabel funktionierte nicht. Wir konnten die Daten aus dem Telefon auf eine SIM-Karte und von da in ein anderes Telefon übertragen - das war der einfachste Weg.
problem_en: The data from an old phone should be transferred to a new one. The data cable did not work. We could transfer the data from the phone to a SIM card and from there to another phone - that was the easiest way.

problem: Fortsetzung vom 6.11.2014: Er wurde nochmals untersucht, konnte aber wegen mehrerer Defekte (Heizspirale unterbrochen, Motor defekt) nicht mehr repariert werden.
problem_en: Continued on 6.11.2014: It was re-examined, but could not be repaired due to several defects (heat spiral interrupted, engine defective).

problem: Musikverstärker mit Subwoofer zeigte keinerlei Lebenszeichen mehr. Wir konnten zwei defekte Sicherungen auswechseln und somit das Gerät wieder in Gang setzen. Leider funktionierte der Subwoofer nicht, was offenbar die Ursache für die durchgebrannten Sicherungen war. Optisch war nichts zu entdecken und ein paar „Verdachtsmessungen“ brachten auch keinen Erfolg. Vielleicht kommt das Gerät nochmal mit Schaltplan wieder. Schaltplan für weitere Untersuchungen fehlt.
problem_en: Music amplifiers with subwoofer did not show any signs of life anymore. We were able to replace two defective fuses and thus put the device back into operation. Unfortunately, the subwoofer did not work, which was obviously the cause of the fuses burned. Visually, there was nothing to discover and a few "suspicious measurements" did not succeed either. Maybe the device comes back again with schematics. Schematic for further investigations is missing.

problem: Fortsetzung vom 20.11.2014: Wir konnten ein loses Kabel wieder anlöten und versuchten, ein Zahnrad in der Mechanik zu wechseln, aber das Ersatzteil passte leider nicht. Wir probieren es beim nächsten Mal mit einem anderen Ersatzteil nochmal.
problem_en: Continuation from 20.11.2014: We were able to solder a loose cable again and tried to change a gear in the mechanics, but unfortunately the spare part did not fit. We try again next time with another spare part.

Ein Abzieher konnte nicht angesetzt werden. Danach schmirgeln und fetten/ölen. Auch die Diode zur v-Reduzierung musste getauscht werden.

For opening a good instruction from ifixit (URL below). The motor axis could be tapped even after 36 h action of WD40, among other things, only with relatively strong hammer strokes from the plain bearing. A puller could not be used. Then shimmer and grease/oil. Also the diode for v reduction had to be replaced.

problem: Schmutz im Bereich des Touch Sensors. lässt sich nicht einschalten. Die Lampe besitzt einen grossen Akku (2x 18650), wird per Touch bedient und ist intern vorbildlich und schön aufgebaut, wohl auch dem entsprechend teuer. Habe die Lampe demontiert, Akku und LEDs waren OK. Ohne Gehäuse/Lampenschirm hat die Touch-Bedienung funktioniert! Ursache war etwas (nicht sichtbarer) Schmutz, der sich in der Rille um den Touchbereich oben auf dem Lampenschirm befand. Ich habe diese Rille sachte ausgekratzt, jetzt geht wieder alles.
problem_en: The lamp has a large battery (2x 18650), is operated by touch and is internally exemplary and beautifully constructed, probably also expensive. I dismantled the lamp, battery and LEDs were OK. Without housing/lampshade the touch operation worked! The reason was something (not visible) dirt, which was in the groove around the touch area on top of the lampshade. I scratched this groove gently, now everything goes again.

problem: Gear to connect gearbox to conveyor belt roller is smashed, unrecoverable; calculator power wire broke off from soldering on battery terminal; multiple broken plastic struts and supports; stripped screw; Cracked, aged plastic; handheld scanner missing. Impact to conveyor belt side of machine; non-functional conveyor belt, unpowered calculator; missing belt. Removed gearbox as it probably impacted the calculator wire's disconnection at the point of impact, and it is not able to function without a new gear and new support structures. Owner is aware and gearbox is included with the toy in a separate bag, for potential re-connection if a new gear is fashioned. Soldered calculator power wire to battery terminal, now functional. Performs math operations just fine and stays on/turns off as directed. Cleaned out battery corrosion as well as possible from the battery compartment. Super-glued major crack in plastic casing but unable to seal a second crack. Sewed & installed new fabric belt for rollers, which can be operated manually by pulling/pushing gently. Epoxy and superglue on plastic strut holding conveyor roller in place. Screws from broken, non-functional supports/connections have been removed and put in the parts bag. Plastic was wiped down with alcohol wipes to remove yellowing. Owner was advised of all repairs and changes. A scanner from another cash register toy could be used with this toy, but would need a new scanner mount on the side of the machine. Owner was advised conveyor mechanism is delicate and does not roll all the way through - original belt was likely plastic, the fabric has a seam that gets caught on a full roll-through.

problem: Aus www: ein 0.01µF Kondensator ist für diesen Fehler verantwortlich. Anlasser läuft nur noch "Vollgas", keine Regelung möglich. Den C habe ich getauscht. Aufwand bedeuteten die Kohlen in dem frei aufgebauten Schiebepotentiometer. Die bestellten Kohlen konnten nicht o. weiteres eingebaut werden, sie zerbrachen beim Versuch. Nach einem privaten Expertentipp habe ich ersatzweise aus einem Bleistift die Mine extrahiert, sie passt mit D=2 mm genau. Daraus wurden 2 Stummel auf passende Länge gesägt, geschliffen und in den (noch teilgefüllten) alten Kohlenhalter eingesetzt. Unverzichtbares Hilfsmittel war eine 2 cm breite Folie, die zum Einbau (zur Fixierung der Kohlestummel) um den Schieber gelegt und danach entfernt wurde. Fotos bei uh._x000d_ Mit neuerer Erkenntnis können die Originalkohlen eingebaut werden, indem der Metallstreifen hinten im Schieber entfernt und die Verdickung der Kohle im Inneren des Schiebers zu liegen kommt - Achtung, winzige Federn! Für diese Variante wird die Reparierbarkeit mit 7 bewertet; das Einsetzen der Stummel war deutlich schwieriger.
problem_en: From www: a 0.01μF capacitor is responsible for this error. Starter runs only "full gas", no regulation possible. I changed the C. Effort meant the coals in the freely constructed sliding potentiometer. The ordered coals could not be installed or further, they broke during the experiment. After a private expert tip I extracted the mine from a pencil by replacement, it fits exactly with D=2 mm. From this 2 stubs were sawed on appropriate length, ground and inserted into the (still partially filled) old coal holder. Indispensable aid was a 2 cm wide foil, which was placed for installation (for fixation of the coal stub) around the slide and then removed. Photos at uh._x000d_ With more recent knowledge the original charcoal can be installed, by removing the metal strip at the back of the slider and the thickening of the coal in the inside of the slider to lie - Attention, tiny springs! For this variant the repairability is evaluated with 7; the insertion of the stubble was clearly difficult.

problem: Das Problem besteht tatsächlich. Zuvor wurden vom Eigentümer innenliegende Kunststoffzahnräder ausgetauscht, die "zerbröselt" waren. Dadurch falsche Synchronisation der beweglichen Teile. _x000d_ Verkettung der Fäden funktioniert nicht. Habe das senkrecht stehende Kegelrad unter der Spulenkapsel um ca. 8° nach links versetzt. Verkettung funzt jetzt in allen 3 Stichlagen. Aber evtl jetzt Problem: zu grosser Transport bei Stichlänge 0. _x000d_ Die Maschine konnte nur mit Unterstützung eines Fachreparateurs in Wehr instandgesetzt und justiert werden. Sie hatte diverse weitere Problemfelder, die alle in einem teilweise "zyklischen" Verfahren behoben wurden: 1) Nadelmittelstellung 2) Abstand Nadel - Greifer 3) Synchronisation der Zickzack-Bewegung (setzte schon ein, als die Nadel noch im Stoff steckte). 4) Greifer-Kegelzahnräder für Greifer-/Verkettungszeitpunkt 5) Fadenspannung unten 6) Fadenspannung oben - diese wurde komplett demontiert und wieder justiert.
problem_en: The problem actually exists. Previously, the owner replaced internal plastic gears that were "broken". Due to this incorrect synchronization of the moving parts. _x000d_ Chaining of the threads does not work. I moved the vertical bevel wheel under the coil capsule by approx. 8° to the left. Chaining now works in all 3 stitch layers. But possibly now problem: too large transport at stitch length 0. _x000d_ The machine could only be repaired and adjusted with the help of a repairer in Wehr. It had several other problem areas, all fixed in a partly "cyclic" procedure: 1) Needle center position 2) Distance needle - gripper 3) Synchronization of the zigzag movement (used already when the needle was still in the fabric). 4) Gripper-crew gears for gripper/chain time point 5) Thread tension below 6) Thread tension above - this was completely dismantled and adjusted again.

problem: Bottom paper tray feeder: glue holding plastic gear on feeder shaft had failed. Gear was spinning freely on the shaft and was no longer transfer power to the secondary roller/feeder shaft. _x000d_ Top scanner feeder: rollers had some dust/gunk on them. Nothing too noticeable but cleaning them all resulted in the feeder working well again, so I can assume that was the problem. Bottom paper tray feeder not working (not feeding any paper). Also top scanner feeder inconsistently feeding paper and/or jamming a lot. Bottom paper tray feeder: Super-glued the gear back onto the shaft. Could not test the feeder to verify the fix since the printer was out of ink (printer refused to do anything without ink), but customer will test at home. They were shown where the problem was and advised to try epoxying the gear back on if the superglue fails. _x000d_ Top scanner feeder: cleaned all rollers with No Flash & a Q-tip.
problem_en: Bottom paper tray feeder: glue holding plastic gear on feeder shaft had failed. Gear was spinning freely on the shaft and was no longer transfer power to the secondary roller/feeder shaft. _x000d_ Top scanner feeder: rollers had some dust/gunk on them. Nothing too noticeable but cleaning them all resulted in the feeder working well again, so I can assume that was the problem. Bottom paper tray feeder not working (not feeding any paper). Could not test the feeder to verify the fix since the printer was out of ink (printer refused to do anything without ink), but customer will test at home. problem: connecteur d'alimentation défectueux. ne démarre plus. 1) J'ai testé la batterie (NiMH) et elle était bonne (tension et courant de charge de décharge). _x000d_ 2) J'ai testé le moteur et il était bon (proche de 0 ohm entre les pôles), il a également fonctionné correctement lorsqu'il était alimenté à environ 1,3V DC. _x000d_ 3) J'ai testé l'interrupteur et il était également bon _x000d_ 4) J'en suis venu à suspecter la diode entre le jack d'alimentation et l'alimentation positive mais en refaisant le schéma, elle n'a pas pu être suspectée _x000d_ J'ai ensuite essayé de connecter directement la batterie au moteur en contournant le PCB et j'ai constaté que cela fonctionnait bien. Donc le seul composant restant était le jack d'alimentation ! Ce n'est pas un jack bipolaire, c'est un jack tripolaire et je pense que le problème se situe ici : le 3ème pôle est ouvert (ou fermé) lorsque l'on insère le jack d'alimentation et cela empêche le trimmer de démarrer lorsqu'il est en charge. Soit on le change, soit on "bidouille" un court circuit de ce jack avec 2 cables que l'on fait ressortir du rasoir, peu esthétique mais relativement discret et très efficace et bon marché!_x000d_

Donc le seul composant restant était le jack d'alimentation ! Ce n'est pas un jack bipolaire, c'est un jack tripolaire et je pense que le problème se situe ici : le 3ème pôle est ouvert (ou fermé) lorsque l'on insère le jack d'alimentation et cela empêche le trimmer de démarrer lorsqu'il est en charge. Soit on le change, soit on "bidouille" un court circuit de ce jack avec 2 cables que l'on fait ressortir du rasoir, peu esthétique mais relativement discret et très efficace et bon marché!_x000d_

problem: A small leak in one of the hose connections on the rightmost boiler (domed silver cylinder) when looking from front of the machine. The hose leaking was the hose located at approximately 12:00 when looking from the front of the machine. Leaking when machine is turned on, while the boilers are heating. First I filled the reservoir with water. Then removed the back upper grated panel (removed two torx 20 screws on panel, and two phillips on inner lip at the top of the reservoir alcove. Then removed top panel (removed two deep phillips screws under control panel on the front). This gave good access to view the entire machine, and any potential leak points. Then turned the device on and immediately found water leaking out of aforementioned location._x000d_ _x000d_ Then removed the hose by taking out a small colder pin using a special curved needle. Two old and aged o-rings were found inside, we swapped the order of the o-rings. Tried powering on again but still leaked._x000d_ _x000d_ Advice given was to replace the two o-rings.

problem: Needs OS flashing. Won't switch on. Used a laptop to download firmware, installed Samsung USB driver, installed ODIN firmware flashing tool and followed instructions largely from https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/how-manually-flash-android-5-1-1-lollipop-via-odin-samsung-galaxy-tab-4-8-0-1511518 and got specific firmware from https://galaxyfirmware.com/model/SM-T210/BTU/T210XXBOA3 - Extract (unzip) the SM-T210_BTU_T210XXBOA3......T210XXBOA3.zip file. using WinRAR or 7-Zip._x000d_ Download Odin Tool 3.14.1_x000d_ Extract Odin and open it._x000d_ Reboot Samsung Phone in Download Mode (hold Home + Power + Volume Down buttons / hold Volume Down + Bixby buttons then plug-in cable)_x000d_ Connect you Samsung Phone and wait until you get a BLUE sign in Odin._x000d_ Add the 1 file Samsung firmware (.md5 file) to AP/PDA or 4 files Samsung firmware (AP/BL/CP/CSC) to it's slots._x000d_ Do NOT tick any extra boxes. The only options to be ticked are F.Reset Time and Auto-Reboot._x000d_ Click the start button, wait for Odin to say 'PASS' in a GREEN sign. Once the flash is complete, your phone will reboot, and you can disconnect your phone from the PC.

The only options to be ticked are F.Reset Time and Auto-Reboot._x000d_ Click the start button, wait for Odin to say 'PASS' in a GREEN sign. problem: 5 composants en court-circuit sur la platine de puissance de droite. Deux IGBT IXGR32N60 (mos3 et 4), le pont redresseur de puissance: GBJ2510 , deux diodes zener CMS de 15V (zd10 et 11) La plaque faut sauter le disjoncteur. Des composants doivent être en court-circuit sur une des plaque de l'électrinique de commande. On peut noter sur la carte filtre et alimentation (en haut à droite) qu'une piste cuivre qui sert de fusible est grillée. Cette piste sert de fusible et fond quand il y a un court circuit sur les circuits de puissance. Il faut déterminer quelle carte est fautive et trouver les composants en CC sur cette carte. Il faut enlever la plaque de verre pour visualiser les 3 cartes électroniques. Les 2 cartes avant sont les cartes de puissance des inducteurs droits et gauches. La carte à l'arrière droit est la carte filtre et alimentation. Démonter les 2 cartes avant et les tester sur le secteur 230V en ayant soin de mettre une ampoule de 40 à 100W en série avec un des fils (neutre ou phase). Cette méthode permet de déterminer quelle carte est en CC (court circuit). Si la lampe s'allume brièvement et s'éteint c'est que la carte n'est pas en CC, si la lampe reste allumée vous avez trouvé la carte fautive. Dans mon cas c'est la carte droite. Il faut maintenant trouver les composants fautifs. Pour cela prenez un multimètre et commencer par vérifier les IGBT (IXGR32N60). Si vous tester en position ohmmètre entre les broches 1 et 2 et 1 et 3 vous devez trouver plus de 70ko. Je trouve les 2 IGBT de droite en CC. Il arrive souvent que d'autres composants grillent avec les IGBT. Je trouve le pont GBJ2510 en CC ainsi que deux diodes zener cms zd10 (15v) et zd11 (15). Il faut remplacer ces 5 composants que l'on peut trouver sur internet. Après remplacement des 5 composants le test de la lampe indique que la plaque n'est plus en CC. Après remontage des cartes la plaque fonctionne correctement. Voir photo.

problem: 16th Nov 2019 item37: Bernina 830 sewing machine The foot pedal was reported as not working properly, speed was either off or fast. Further checks showed it only did straight stitch. The straight stitching also had tangles. So 3 problems to solve!! To investigate further, covers were removed. Just take care at this point as mains voltages may be exposed - think safety and disconnect from mains before removing covers. Problem 1: Straight stitch only was down to "sticky" oil preventing the needle left/right mechanism engaging correctly. "Sticky" oil generally indicates the wrong oil has been used at some time, don't use 3in1, WD40 or anything other than sewing machine oil - a one ounce bottle will cost a couple of pounds and will always be useful if you intend to maintain the machine yourself. Cleaning the "sticky" oil requires some patience, meths and cotton buds to slowly clean and free the mechanism. You may need to repeat once or twice to finally clean the bad oil out. Once the mechanism is moving relatively freely, apply som sewing machine oil (just a small drop will do). DON'T be tempted to take things apart, remove grub screws or anything else because unless you understand what you are doing you may completely mess up the timing and your machine will not work without being correctly retimed. Cleaned and oiled, zig zag stitching worked OK Problem 2: tangles during stitching. Well probably a classic issue here. The most important part of your machine is often the overlooked one - the needle! These poor things get used, abused and are still expected to work. In reality a needle lasts for around 6-8hrs of use before it becomes blunt and should be replaced. Add to that the occasional catching for whatever reason on the foot plate and needle bend, get "stubbed" ends that catch on the cotton and yes if you buy cheap you often get cheap, rough poor quality needles that are not fit for purpose. Good brands such a Singer, Schmetz are worth the extra cost and will be reliable. "stubbed" ends will catch cotton and cause tangles, fraying of thread and even braking of thread. bent needles - well problems should be obvious! cheap needles - looking under a microscope I've seen on new needles loose plating(?!), badly shaped ends and eyes with rough edges - all symptoms of poor stitching. For this machine the needle was bent as well as rough. Replacing with a new Singer needle and all was well. Problem 3: The foot pedal. Immediate suspect was the capacitors. These were replace with the same type (very important to get the correct rating type as a replacement look for something like X2 or Y1 and only replace with the same). Once replaced and cleaned the machine speed worked correctly again. Whilst inside the foot pedal make sure cables are properly secured, not frayed or cracked and once all is put back together don't forget that PAT test for safety before returning to the owner. Roger.

"Sticky" oil generally indicates the wrong oil has been used at some time, don't use 3in1, WD40 or anything other than sewing machine oil - a one ounce bottle will cost a couple of pounds and will always be useful if you intend to maintain the machine yourself. Cleaning the "sticky" oil requires some patience, meths and cotton buds to slowly clean and free the mechanism. You may need to repeat once or twice to finally clean the bad oil out. Once the mechanism is moving relatively freely, apply som sewing machine oil (just a small drop will do). DON'T be tempted to take things apart, remove grub screws or anything else because unless you understand what you are doing you may completely mess up the timing and your machine will not work without being correctly retimed. Cleaned and oiled, zig zag stitching worked OK Problem 2: tangles during stitching. Well probably a classic issue here. The most important part of your machine is often the overlooked one - the needle! These poor things get used, abused and are still expected to work. In reality a needle lasts for around 6-8hrs of use before it becomes blunt and should be replaced. Add to that the occasional catching for whatever reason on the foot plate and needle bend, get "stubbed" ends that catch on the cotton and yes if you buy cheap you often get cheap, rough poor quality needles that are not fit for purpose. Good brands such a Singer, Schmetz are worth the extra cost and will be reliable. "stubbed" ends will catch cotton and cause tangles, fraying of thread and even braking of thread. bent needles - well problems should be obvious! cheap needles - looking under a microscope I've seen on new needles loose plating(?!), badly shaped ends and eyes with rough edges - all symptoms of poor stitching. For this machine the needle was bent as well as rough. Replacing with a new Singer needle and all was well. Problem 3: The foot pedal. Immediate suspect was the capacitors. These were replace with the same type (very important to get the correct rating type as a replacement look for something like X2 or Y1 and only replace with the same). Once replaced and cleaned the machine speed worked correctly again. Whilst inside the foot pedal make sure cables are properly secured, not frayed or cracked and once all is put back together don't forget that PAT test for safety before returning to the owner. Roger.

problem: (Model believed to be obsolete) no longer heats up after a minor fall, On testing the (premium irons) digital control panel lights up and bleeps on pressing buttons but Iron plate doesn't heat up, there was a minor crack of little significance to the body where the iron had landed after a fall which had been half caught and then released due to being burned. Two security screws (split spade - the only ones - all other screws normal) and use of a spudger removed the back panel. A screw accessible from behind the back panel and two under the two steam control buttons which needed to be removed first, allows the top panel on the handle to be removed revealing the two control boards marked with stickers with part numbers. One controller board with an LCD panel and rubberised buttons and one relay and transistor control board. Both are contained in their own plastic housing which were sealed and potted with rubber sealent to maintain as water proofed. Everything in this iron was a bit of a surprise (compared with other cheaper irons i've worked on) the unit was very well constructed and I don't think I've ever seen and item so well built for repairability, everything was connected via removable plugs and sockets or terminal blocks. There was even easy access to the hot plate with a bit more deconstruction. Further testing both powered (under caution) and unpowered showed the hotplate was ok, the LCD control system was ok, all the circuitry received power, but power was not delivered back to the hot plate via the relay in the relay control board, making that the primary suspect. Searching online revealed a telephone number for spare parts for Russell Hobbs UK customer and technical service help and spare parts line and also for a third party supplier Partsmaster. Both were able to supply consumables such as filters for the steam chamber or even a new power flex but Russell Hobbs said the unit was now obsolete and they did not provide controller spare parts for that iron. When pressed as to if it were possible to obtain spare controller parts for ANY iron? They replied they didn't do that kind of spare part. I asked why they had a spare parts department and phone number they said they do provide parts for other types of products. This was a huge disappointment as it essentially means no electrical fault on ANY Russell Hobbs Iron requiring spare parts with the exception of a power flex is repairable. Attempts were made to find the spare from other third party sources but non was evident. The iron was fully deconstructed and photos taken for Restarters.net I would estimate the value of the spare part as less than £10 as a mass produced item. So the whole iron which should have been repairable will now go to be recycled for want of this simple spare part. It might be possible to deconstruct the control board and investigate the fault at board level but this would risk creating a repair that is no longer water tight and create potential unnecessary safety liability issues for the client and so the repair was not pursued further. ooo-xxx.

problem: 16th Nov 2019 item?: Shredder The motor had a burnt out winding indicated by darkened enamel on the copper windings and an open circuit winding. Always worth checking each winding resistance with a meter on ohms range (ensure no power connected first!). All windings should show a very similar resistance, sometimes one winding (or several) may be a quite different lower resistance indicating shorted windings, or a short circuit (0 ohms) or open circuit. Tip: If windings seem OK, it's worth checking all connections and switch with meter set to ohms range (again ensure no power connected first!) and cleaning paper particles out. Motor windings can look overheated but may still work and cleaning will reduce overheating. Shredders do get hammered!! Don't forget that PAT test before returning to the owner, think safe. Roger.

problem: The printer paper feed was not working possibly due to the feed roller either worn or needed cleaning to improve friction. The printer was showing an out of paper signal when it only had a few sheets in the tray. Putting a larger stack of paper and the feed mechanism was working. The printer cartridges were replaced, and the printer worked OK. As time was limiting and it did print OK provided there was a reasonable amount of paper in the tray it was decided not to remove the bottom panel with the risk of causing more damage. What could work is to use a cotton bud possibly on the end of a thin screwdriver and clean the feed roller with spirit or equivalent to improve friction. problem: Mini USB charging port detached from circuit board. After attempts by three Restarters it was successfully resoldered. Micro soldering skills were needed to reattach the port and then a heat gun was used to flow-solder the electrical connections. This is a common failure in cheap electronic items. problem: The owner came with her husband's mobile and a spare battery, the phone was working, but the battery was due for replacement. An attempt to change the battery resulted in a damaged screen, and the participant resorted to buying a new phone after confirming with her husband that his data was backed up on the cloud. This was a fix that would take too much time to do it properly at the event. The resulting damage to the screen meant the participant got emotional and panicked, which is why the three restarters and two hosts, plus two venue volunteers all stayed two hours longer trying to sort out the situation, mediating the participant's panic. We learned that we have to have a disclaimer form for every participant to sign, stating that they understand that it is not guaranteed that a fixing attempt will be successful and that their item could be damaged even further by attempting to fix it.

problem: 16th Nov 2019 item7: 40" flatscreen LCD TV switched mode power supply failed. Warning: do not mess with switched mode power supplies unless you understand the basics of how they work and particularly the risks. Parts of the PCB WILL be at mains or even higher voltages and capacitors may hold high voltages even when mains is disconnected. Tips for checking switched mode power supply: - Remove mains first and leave for 10-15mins to allow capacitors to discharge OR if you know how to safety check with a multimeter then proceed. - flatten a clean staple free cardboard box to lay the TV screen down on - this makes it easy to move the TV around during the investigations and also keeps the screen protected from scratches. - Remove the back keeping screws safely in a pot - you may need to remove the stand / wall brackets first. - Identify the switched mode power supply PCB - it's usually quite easy as it will have transformers, capacitors and other larger components some with heatsinks. The PCB should be marked with warnings such as "HOT" or "DANGER" and there may well be a white hatched area - this indicates mains voltages present. - be aware some metal parts may still have residual voltages present - check with you multimeter on volts range. - check the board for clues such as overheating, fuses that have blown etc. Semiconductors such as diodes / FETs can fail and crack or show small holes. If this is visible you can identify and replace such components (easily said, not always so easy to do!) OR simply purchase a replacement board of the same type and version. In this particular case, I found two failed diodes marked Q165A (full device type is RBQ10B65A) - they were short circuit. I replaced them with similar higher spec devices Vishay 12CWQ10FN and the TV worked fine. - If nothing obvious is found check other boards for faults -was the TV dropped? has it been given a hard life? Many faults I find in electronic equipment are mechanical - worn switch, mechanically poor connector mountings causing broken PCB connections or lifted and broken copper pad. For the latter forget reflowing the joint, use enamel covered wire to create a more rugged connection over the break. Happy hunting! and don't forget making sure all earth straps/metal shields are correctly replaced and tightened before refitting covers. Lastly remember to PAT test before returning to the owner, think safe. Roger.

problem: 16th Nov 2019item?: Technosonic LCD3201 TV The TV would not switch on. The standby switch had not been working for a while so the owner had turned the TV on/off using the mains socket switch. This was described as sometimes working but if it did not then the mains socket switch would be turned on/ff several times to persuade the TV to turn on. Eventually the TV failed to turn on at all. OK, the first point to make here is that turning on/off several times at the mains socket switch is not recommended. The issue is that it probably overstresses the TV power supply and other components which will have to deal with repeated inrush/outrush currents. The standby switch on any device will turn it on and off in a more controlled manner. Anyway lets explain this fix. Warning: TVs contain switched mode power supplies so unless you understand the basics of how they work and particularly the risks do not mess with them. Parts of the PCB WILL be at mains or even higher voltages and capacitors may hold high voltages even when mains is disconnected. First step was to disconnect from the mains for safety, then remove the back to expose the circuit boards. Looking at the standby switch, the plastic button had partly broken and it no longer reliably operated the PCB mounted on/off switch. This was fixed by placing a small piece of heatshrink tubing around the switch to guide the damaged button to the correct place. The button now functioned and the familiar quiet operating click could be heard. Next the TV was powered on. The button functioned but the TV would not turn and remained in standby. Time to get the multimeter out to check voltages on the standby switch. This appeared to work correctly. After tracing the on/off signal back to the switched mode power supply board (take care, high voltages here!) it seemed the signal was not getting through to enable the power supplies. Fortunately the connector functions were marked on the PCB and it was easy to work out which pin enabled the power supply. Now a little trick to check power supplies. The enable line typically needs to be connected to ground to enable the 5V/12V whatever supplies to the TV. So turn off the TV, disconnect the mains and carefully remove all connectors to the power supply board. Next find something like a 100ohm resistor and connect the enable line to ground (OK you could just use a wire but the resistor restricts any current to a sensible amount if you get this wrong!!). Now connect the TV to the mains and with a multimeter check the relevant supply voltages are present. In this case all was correct, so that told me either another board was faulty and causing the power supply to go into protect mode (shutdown) or that indeed there was something wrong with the standby circuit on another PCB. Recalling the repeated turn on/turn off the TV had suffered and the fact the standby enable line to the power supply did not fuction correctly I suspected the PCB was faulty. There were no obvious problems and in the absence of a circuit diagram or service manual we looked for a replacement PCB. Luckily one was found at just over £10 inc P+P. What a find! The owner decided it was worth the chance so the board was ordered, duly arrived and was installed. The TV switched on and all was well. I admit it was quite a "hunch" to be lucky enough to identify the faulty PCB but it worked and another 40" TV lived to play another day. PCB was purchased here https://spares2repair.co.uk/ and no I don't have anything to do with this company! Once all is put back together don't forget that PAT test for safety before returning to the owner. One final work, only purchase the same board type and version and if possible check of a photo of the actual board you will receive first for overheating and other visible faults. Roger.

So turn off the TV, disconnect the mains and carefully remove all connectors to the power supply board. Next find something like a 100ohm resistor and connect the enable line to ground (OK you could just use a wire but the resistor restricts any current to a sensible amount if you get this wrong!!). Now connect the TV to the mains and with a multimeter check the relevant supply voltages are present. In this case all was correct, so that told me either another board was faulty and causing the power supply to go into protect mode (shutdown) or that indeed there was something wrong with the standby circuit on another PCB. Recalling the repeated turn on/turn off the TV had suffered and the fact the standby enable line to the power supply did not fuction correctly I suspected the PCB was faulty. There were no obvious problems and in the absence of a circuit diagram or service manual we looked for a replacement PCB. Luckily one was found at just over £10 inc P+P. What a find! The owner decided it was worth the chance so the board was ordered, duly arrived and was installed. The TV switched on and all was well. I admit it was quite a "hunch" to be lucky enough to identify the faulty PCB but it worked and another 40" TV lived to play another day. PCB was purchased here https://spares2repair.co.uk/ and no I don't have anything to do with this company! Once all is put back together don't forget that PAT test for safety before returning to the owner. One final work, only purchase the same board type and version and if possible check of a photo of the actual board you will receive first for overheating and other visible faults. Roger.

problem: 16th Nov 2019 item29: HMV valve radiogram chassis This was a very old radiogram chassis pre 1960's using valves (no transistors or FETs!). First comment is that these are dangerous with high voltages on exposed parts (300-400V and sometimes higher so if you do not understand how they work and cannot identify danger areas DO NOT DABBLE!! Second comment is that this repair is not something to do at a repair cafe event unless you can guarantee no-one but yourself can touch anything either accidentally or deliberately. I took the chassis home: - step 1, get the service manual - step 2, clean the dust off and check correct valves in place and look for failed components - old capacitors are typical failures. They become leaky and loose their capacitance. All seemed remarkably well given the age! One valve was incorrect and removed. This left 2 missing valves. They were in fact the push pull audio output stage valves type HN309. These are somewhat unusual as they have a 12.6V heater - my hunch is that they were used in old valve car radios operating from a 12V battery. HN309 are triode/pentodes (2 valves in one) and like rocking horse you know what to find but after some investigation I found a very similar type LN309 and further cross referencing identified a more common PCL83 as a potential alternative after comparing specs (see here at the Valve Museum for valve information http://www.r-type.org/) - step 3, Decided to fit a modern mains lead - the old leads were not in a good state. - step 4, I performed a 250V insulation test on the mains transformer and also between primary and secondary windings (looking for breakdown of the enamel coating on windings) - all was well. In this case I repeated at 500V and again all was well. Also checked mains switch wiring was working using a multimeter switched to measure resistance. Again all was well, particularly no shorts. - step 5, I decided to switch on!! even with 2 valves missing. Switching on was performed at the mains socket, with the unit on/off switch already set to on. No nasty smells or pops!! The valves glowed correctly, the tuner bulbs came on and all appeared well even after 5 minutes warm up. The next step was back to the owner to purchase 2 PCL83 valves. These duly came some weeks later and were plugged in. On switch on all again was well and the 2 new valves glowed correctly. The next step is to find a suitable 8ohm speaker, in the mean time I'll test carefully with a signal generator and oscilloscope. Having the circuit diagram makes life easy, just remember this is valve equipment not low voltage modern stuff so take care as the voltages present can be fatal!! I'll update when I've made further progress. Roger.

problem: Record player. When switching on the record player, placing a record on the turntable, and switching it down to 'Start' or 'Auto' mode, the pickup (reading) arm was supposed to automatically swing into position and the disc to begin spinning, but this did not happen. Opening up the case, we found that the motor was spinning freely when the switch was in the 'Stop' position, but then appeared to slowly and unevenly judder around in steps when the other switch positions applied a clutch to the motor. With all of the system consisting of just one motor and a highly complex assembly of mechanical/clockwork/transmission parts, we could not identify the fault after an hour, with no online help available for this decades-old piece of tech, and suspected that finding the faulty component would require spending all day dismantling and studying the mechanism.

problem: DAB not working. Another restarter had attempted to open the radio but had been flummoxed by a screw for which they didn't have the right driver. I tried it with the owner and found it was working including on DAB. The issue was that the DAB reception was very poor where were and I suspect in the owners flat (many tall concrete building likely blocking signals and creating lots of signal reflections and crosspaths). So the radio was showing Unavailable and this was wrongly interpreted as the radio malfunctioning rather than the DAB signal being unavailable. We did manage to listen to a few DAB stations. I also suspect that reception may be better/worse depending on the multiplex on which a station belongs to.

Tip: don't throw away your old power adaptors, they can be recycled for just such problems as this. Just confirm the voltage is correct and that the current rating is equal to (or exceeds) the failed adaptor. problem: Works/powers-up but now loses signal on some stations. The frequency is stable, but the sound is replaced by white noise. This happens when the radio warms up. A dusting is required. It may need finding a suitable repair shop. We shared the link to the Repair Directory. f it's possible to advise Frances. It's very likely that most / All the electroletic capacitors have failed, they may pass an ESR test but in effect act as high value resistors, some will cause much more current to flow in the valve, which can cause whats knows as 'red plating' this will eventually cause the valve fail, or worse cause the HT or output Transformers to fail (depending upon what circuit the valve is in). at which pont it's extramly difficult to souce a spares once capacitors replaced it's likely to require realignment of both the local oscillator and the IF stage(s) a signal generator is required. and likely last another 70 years :)

problem: Client unable to make work as it requires specialist cables and Power supply, The unit requires the use of an adaptor box that was restrictively expensive, The manuals gave no information about wiring the unit. The unit was found to operate correctly with a 12v DC PSU and appropraite RS485 wiring connections to the DVR unit. The client was advised on the wiring diagramme and how to derive the 12v supply from the internal ATX style powersupply of the DVR unit.

problem: The USB chargeable bike light had stopped charging, so the owner had peeled away the silicon overmoulding the wires. One of the wires was visibly detached from the USB charging connector, so that was soldered on by one of the fixers. This did not seem to have solved the problem, and as the other repairs moved on, the bike light waited for a spare moment to be looked at again. Another fixer picked up the repair and, looking closely, with a loupe, and prodding with a multimeter for the signs of life throught the remaining silicon overmoulding, it was discovered that the other wire connection is corroded. The repairer extended the wire, soldered it to the extension and to the USB charging plate, and the light was now charging and working properly. As the light clips around the handlebar when in use and the USB charging connector is designed as a part of the grip holder, the light will need overmoulding the connections with something like Sugru, something that waterproofs it, providing flexibility and allowing for further repairs if needed. Overall it is a fiddly job, but these lights are comparatively expensive to buy and very good when they work. The 3rd party parts required were wires for the extension and Sugru for overmoulding.

Connections around the small bulb used for this were found to be corroding. The seal around the small transparent window next to the bulb was theorised to be leaking steam onto the bulb, and so the bulb was repositioned further up the handle. This solved the problem, while altering a faulty feature of the kettle to make it safer - the glow was now in the handle, but not corroding. The user was advised that if the problem returned, this part of the wiring would probably have to be cut out and bypassed.

problem: Not working. The resistance is dead. To expensive to replace because the resistor is welded to the container. The kettle was not working. We tried to open it, it was quite easy. We analyse a few components, trying to find a thermal fuse. No thermal fuse... Thus we tested the resistance : it was broken. We thought about replacing it, but the resistor is welded to the container, thus, it is too expensive. I contacted the brand to ask them why there is no thermal fuse and why the resistor is welded, since the kettle cost more than 80€. They answered that their "products are designed with care and by aiming for as long a lifespan as possible". Maybe we should go further ?

problem: The steam cleaner was tripping the user's RCD at home. The machine was dismantled, signs of leakage and corrosion were observed on a parting line between a bolted-flange boiler, the item was given a fail by a portable appliance tester, and further testing found it to be short-circuiting to earth somewhere. By methodically disconnecting and testing for leakage, the problem was isolated to the heating element, which was found to be corroding. As the heaing element was soldered into the boiler and not replaceable, the entire boiler would have to be replaced at a significant part cost, and the great majority of the appliance's embodied energy. Whether to choose part replacement was left up to the user.

problem: Plunge saw. The circular saw worked sometimes, but cut out intermittently. We theorised this to be due to a slow buildup of damp & fine sawdust over several years of use, even though it was used with a bag, which could have been causing short circuits. We opened up the casing as far as we could, which was just all but a section immediately around the motor, then brushed, scraped & vacuumed out the visible old sawdust deposits. With the motor windings inaccessible, the user was advised to find an electrical contact cleaning fluid/spray and run it through there if possible, or apply compressed air.

problem: The compressor had stopped pumping and started making loud rattling noises. This was guessed to be a broken nylon gear, but on dis-assembly the fault was even more impressive - the gears were metal, but a cast-metal flange holding one of them in place as it drove a piston, had fractured all the way across and this arm snapped off. On closer inspection it appeared that there was a small ~1mm diameter bubble in the casting on the line of this fracture, which probably initiated it due to fatigue from the cyclic stress.

problem: The blender was not starting. A small plastic part on the jug that would toggle the switch in the base was found to have snapped off. problem: The user brought along their bread maker from two months ago with a replacement drive belt, and we helped them to fit the belt. The belt supplied was not an appropriate fit for the machine - what websites were supplying was a 61cm timing belt with trapezoidal grooves perpendicular to the belt, as used on cars and printers, while the motor drive pulley on this machine had grooves parallel to the belt, more similar to those on washing machines, and this belt was extremely tight to fit given the plastic driven pulley. One repairer still managed to make it fit, but in doing so removed a screw that was supposed to be locking the pulley onto a flat on the drive shaft. In actuality, the pulley was seized onto the shaft, and we weren't able to remove it to make fitting the belt easier, so the user has been advised to bring it back if ever the pulley slips and the stirrer stops turning again, but the machine turned fine with the new belt so we don't expect an issue any time soon.

problem: Stopped turning on after I think I ran it for too long with dough in it. Power is fine as the scale still turns on. Screen shows [----] when you try to run motor. problem: Bosch Rotek 37 Lawn Mower motor if it starts cuts out almost immediately and won't start for a couple of minutes. Motor Thermal cutout switch suspected in first instance after testing cable and main power switch. replacement thermal cutout would only have been about £10.50 inc VAT However further investigation revealed Thermal switch was kicking in because of a Damaged Motor, Main switch had also already been replaced by client at a cost of around £10 Damaged Motor: Brushes in good condition, direct drive of motor and continuity testing on commutator coils revealed some coils approx (40%) were showing open circuit. Replacement cost of motor discovered to be too high, prices online ranging from about £102-£115 for the replacement inc VAT excluding P&P the motor could only be supplied as an assembly of parts which included parts that were not at fault, e.g. Timing belt, cogs, thermal cutout, bearings etc supply of such a motor ought not to really be more than about £30. Cost of buying a new identical lawnmower is only £135. Client advised to buy a new one and consider buying the same model but use the old one as spares for future possible faults. (blade, thermal switch, main switch, collection bucket, cable, etc) Or find a make and model with cheaper available spare parts.

problem: Blown Fuse. Owner reported that something fell onto the treadmill while it was being used which prevented the surface you run on from moving. Treadmill was no longer powering on, even after the obstruction was removed. Repairer opened up the casing and replaced a blown fuse. Treadmill is working again. ISSUE: Fuse was not user-replaceable, (soldered onto printed circuit board) RESOLUTION: Fitted an "in-line fuse holder" which enabled replacement fuse to be fitted. ( https://cpc.farnell.com/unbranded/787-408/20x5mm-in-line-fuse-holder/dp/FF01016 refers) ISSUE: After replacing fuse the treadmill would not power up. We eventually figured out that the safety key was missing. (The safety key is a magnet attached to a string that's attached via a string to a band that goes around the runner's wrist. If they fall over the magnet disengages from the control panel and the treadmill cuts out) RESOLUTION: Found a safety key design on www.thingiverse.com and 3D printed one. (one of the attached images refers). It's a plastic holder for a neodymium magnet.

problem: The internal lithium-ion cell of this battery-bank has been worn out by repeated deep discharging, and no longer holds any significant charge. This is replaceable, but the cheapest equivalent part that we could find from a supplier on eBay cost more than an entire new charger! The charger casing initially seemed like it could only be opened by clips from the outside, with no visible screws, but this got stuck part-way. After very gently prying up the Photovoltaic (PV) cell, which had been untouched for fear of breaking it, some screws were revealed. The PV cell had been held down with some nasty cheap double-sided tape, which gets warped in opening and never goes back on exactly the same way as it was originally constructed. The li-ion cell is significantly under-sized for its available cavity, even if it were to bulge, and finding an exact replacement for these is rare, so a slightly larger one would be a likely option. These proprietary flat cells can be tricky to find due to being listed in some very odd sizes. For example, this was a "705475" cell (7mm x 54mm x 75mm).

Using sandpaper to clean the contact point between kettle and base; also didn't make any difference.. problem: Initial issue: intermittently not working and would hum but blades would barely turn or not at all. At the repair event, we took it apart starting with the plastic clips holding the outer "cage". We noticed it was dusty, the main rod attaching to the blades was rusted, and the blades turned but were stiff. I had oiled it at home but not taken it apart. We continued disassembly, next removing the fan blades. They took a firm and steady pull to get off the main pole. Be careful here, because the plastic can crack around where it threads onto the pole. Mine did and we had to glue it. Next, we removed the 2 nuts and washers holding the back of the "cage" onto the fan. From there, the next disassembly was to get the motor out. I wanted to check the electronics and see if anything looked bad. We removed the bolts holding the legs/base and that allowed the motor to slide out. We had to flex the plastic to get it out. there are also 2 metal tabs that the bolts screw into, acting as nuts. make sure not to lose those. Once we pulled out the motor, someone came over to help who was familiar w similar fans. He suggested we lubricate the bearings both at the front and back of the rotating pole. Everything just looked old and rusty, but nothing was super messed up. We used deoxit to lube the parts, and it made a huge difference. We also krazy glued the part of the fan blade assembly that we'd inadvertently broken during disassembly. Lastly, we scraped off some of the rust from the main pole near where the blades attach. When reassembling, make sure the base is pointing in the right direction. Make sure you screw the base bolts into the metal tabs. when reattaching the fan blades, make sure the plastic gaps line up with the little perpendicular metal stoppers that stick out from the pole. After reassembling some, we tested and saw that the fan ran quietly and well. After full reassembly, the same was true. lubing the back bearing was important for long term repair! I lubed only the front initially but it wasn't enough.

problem: . When we arrived, a Volunteer (Tom) showed us how to use a multimeter in order to determine that yes, our lamp had a short. First we checked the cord connections to the bulb socket and re-connected them to make sure they were tight and clean. The multimeter indicated that there was still a problem, though, so we took the lamp apart and found that the entire wire needed replacing. We did this, ensuring that the ground wire and the live wire were consistently threaded throughout. We left happily with a working lamp. First, make sure you have the right tools: screwdriver, wire strippers/cutters, a replacement wire that is the right length and meant to carry the same voltage, and a multimeter, at bare minimum. Our lamp was a floor lamp with a tall, skinny post that the cable went through. I wished I'd had a long, narrow stick that I could poke into that post. Next, take a good look at your lamp and think about how it might come apart. Look for screws, caps, or other joined places that will provide access to the wire inside the lamp. Think about what might be necessary in order to get the wire out (and in). Visualizing the process before you start is a good idea. There's probably a lot of reference on how to go about fixing the wiring on a lamp online, but it was very helpful to have someone guide us through the process. I never would have thought to use a multimeter, but using it as a way of testing our work instead of just plugging the lamp in was a good thing, it avoided potentially shorting the circuit at the event.

problem: . The appliance no longer generated heat. I suspected it was simply a fuse that had blown. Once the appliance was opened, using testing-meters, it was determined that the thermal fuse had blown. During the time of the clinic, I was able to pick up a new thermal fuse from Al Lescher's in Berkeley. When I returned to the Clinic the old fuse was replaced with a new one ($1.60) and the hot roller appliance was back in working order. The "fix" was quite simple after the diagnosis. The dead fuse was removed and the new thermal fuse was reattached by securing the connecting wires on each end in the same place.

problem: . We took apart the motor for the clock flipping mechanism and were able to determine which gear wasn't catching. Someone on the call was able to identify this path because the final gear, the one that turns the time dial, could be turned by hand and it shouldn't have been able to. The final gear sits in a sleeve that has another gear on it and it was spinning within that sleeve but shouldn't have been. Putting a bit of epoxy on it fixed it! Of course in the process of fixing it I broke one of the soldered points off so I had to purchase a soldering iron and re-attach it. But now it's working perfectly! Up until this event I just thought it was the motor slowing down but someone pointed out that because it's an AC motor it's driven by the current and if the motor is going, it's going at the correct speed. I had been putting WD-40 in but that wasn't helping. Knowing that this AC motor was an on/off type of thing, i.e., they can't slow down, they work or they don't, meant that we knew it was in the gears which isolated the problem.

problem: . The microwave turntable wasn't turning, so I had purchased a replacement motor over a year ago and brought it with me to the event. We replaced the motor and now the turntable turns. Yay! Changing the motor was easy, but getting the case/housing off the microwave was challenging. On the bottom of the microwave, there was a covering right over the motor, but we didn't think we could open it since it required cutting metal to do so. To get the case off, we needed a special tool (Security Torx screwdriver, which is a 6-sided star-shaped screwdriver with a pin in it) and luckily (amazingly), someone at the Fixit Clinic had one. We also used a regular Phillips screwdriver. We kept liberating parts of the case and finding that we had to unscrew more screws to get to the area we needed. (Also, it's a bit intimidating working with electric wires and stuff but we just avoided touching those.) After a lot of work, we got the whole case off of the microwave, but none of that was necessary after all. EXCEPT, by opening the case, we found some super secret instructions taped onto the microwave underneath the case, so it DID tell us what to do! It turned out we COULD get in through the covering right over the motor (so we only needed to open that, not take the entire case off). It turned out, you do just cut the metal, open it up, replace the motor, and then rotate the cover 180 degrees and it has tabs that slip into slots so it can be reused after being cut. The motor itself just needed to be unplugged, rotated, and pulled out. Then we plugged in the new one and rotated it into place. Voila! .

problem: My coffee maker was successfully repaired at the 2/8/25 Boston Building Resources Fixit clinic! The issue with the coffee maker was that the water did not pump. The grinder function and the display still worked, but no water flowed through the system. We took the coffee maker apart to look for the pump. After taking it all the way apart, we realized that there was no pump and the coffee maker used heat alone to push water through the tubing. The issue was that a thermal fuse had blown, and so the circuit for the heating element was broken. A fixer helped me test the connectivity of the fuse and soldered a new wire to bypass the broken fuse (the coffee maker had a second, redundant thermal fuse that had not blown). After this repair step, the coffee maker worked! I have made my coffee with it every morning since. Check the connectivity of the various electrical components first. This was something we could have done very early in the process, and if we had then we would have avoided the cumbersome process of taking the coffee maker apart.

problem: . The problem in my case was the door lock. I blame the implementation of child safety for the problem: if child safety is engaged, kids are still able to turn ON/OFF the appliance. Also if the appliance is ON the same protection engages the lock that is disengaged when OFF. This means that despite child safety a kid can still lock and unlock the door by repetedly clicking the power button. In my case this stress eventually broke the lock, which had to be replaced. Replacing the lock is relatively easy and requires a screwdriver and a pair of pliers. Follow this video https://youtu.be/C2k3w6suShU?t=196 to see how to remove the silicone seal. Once the seal is removed, you unscrew the lock with the 2 screws on the front so you can replace it.

problem: . It took a long time to figure out how to do so, but two fixers were able to partially dismantle the tape deck, remove the UK transmission, and put the original transmission back into the tape deck. Their comment was "They don't make them like they used to." The job was complicated due to the age of the tape deck and lack of a service manual but worth doing because of the quality of the machine. Thanks to their efforts, the tape deck is now working again. I appreciate the fact that the idea behind Fixit Clinics is to involve participants in repairing their items and to teach people how to carry out repairs. However, I think allowances need to be made for the complexity of the item involved, the age of the item, the experience (or lack thereof) of the owner, and the experience of fixers with older models. I would advise attendees to go to Fixit Clinics with hopes of getting their items repaired but feel that they should not have unrealistic expectations. The fixers are wonderful but there are limits to what they can accomplish.

problem: . The waffle iron (my mother's, dating to the 1940s) was disassembled and tested. Preliminarily, since no substitute cords were available, we reinserted the old line into the machine connector. I had already intended to purchase a new cord. The specific electrical requirements of the machine were explained to me, so now I know how to buy the correct cord. We unscrewed the bottom plate, exposing the workings of the lower griddle. When tested, the electrical circuit was fine. The control governing the degree of doneness of the waffle is a completely mechanical thing, running from the knob outside to two little flanges in the middle of the machine which expand or contract with heat. They seemed to be a little stuck (which may account for complaints about overheating). I was advised to sand them down with 600-1200 grit sandpaper to clear the accumulation. I had a lot of questions about cleaning, water, etc. which were answered. So far so good. When we unscrewed the top to expose the upper waffle iron, however, the electrical circuit did not complete. The little white wires leading from the plug to the hot plate part were defective. Diagnosis: the white wires of both top and bottom valves need to be replaced, along with their receptor nuts and bolts; and the heat gauge flanges need to be sanded. It should take an electrical repairman about an hour to do. The going rate for electrical repair in Berkeley is $50-75/ hour. As instructed, I will phone Al Lasher's Electronics on University Avenue for a recommendation. The decision to restore a vintage electrical appliance is based on many factors. The initial assessment at the clinic establishes an upper limit of feasibility and cost. Beyond that, more personal considerations-- environmental, aesthetic and sentimental-- must be taken into account. How much do I loathe sending things to landfill (or having them sent to landfill by whoever inherits the non functional waffle iron)? A lot. Would a second-hand replacement (say from the Oakland Museum White Elephant Sale) be any safer than an appliance (ungrounded, to be sure) which I had had rewired? No. Do I even need a waffle iron? I've lived thirty years with this one in storage. But so many interesting new whole grain waffle recipes are circulating. Could I find a second-hand stove-top iron? As I see it right now, this is a perfectly good waffle iron which can be fixed with a trivial amount of work. Since I lack the skills to fix it myself I have to pay someone to do it. For people retired on a small fixed income in Berkeley everything is ridiculously expensive. I have suggested several times to the North Berkeley Senior Center that it would be good to maintain a list of retired repairmen who would be willing to undertake occasional work for less than the going rate. I have even suggested a program of exchanged work or skills. I can cook or garden expertly in exchange for a small electrical repair. In vain. The unimaginative management is totally uninterested in improving the lives of its members.

problem: . With the generous help of Rob, Brian, and Mike, we eventually removed the cracked screen with a heat gun, and removed and replaced the home button and digitizer attachments that came with my new screen. The removal of the cracked screen took so long that by the time the new screen was on, I decided to pack it up and plug it in another time to attempt to turn it on before securing the adhesive of the new screen. (We were able to see that it responded to charging, pushing the home button, and pushing the power button, so I'm pretty confident it will turn on). The time it took was lengthened by not having gloves or a headlamp, and not having a way immediately on hand, of cleaning the adhesive from the tweezers in order to deal with the tiny screws blocking access to the digitizer attachments. It was lengthened a fair amount by not having the appropriate solution to clean and prep the bare lcd screen as well. I recommend setting aside a good hour and a half for the removal of the old screen and pieces related to it, depending on how cracked the screen is (mine was very thoroughly cracked). I was very glad I'd bought a new screen that came with a kit. The tools in the kit were absolutely necessary, and I could have done with even more guitar picks. The kit was TechOrbits ASIN B0160ERA7U off Amazon. I wish I had researched beforehand what solution Apple uses to clean their bare LCD screens. Iso was not a good choice, and the microfiber cloths were not overly effective due to the foam gasket. I wish I had brought gloves and a headlamp, as well as a cup for screws (thanks Brian!), a container for glass shards, packing tape (thanks Brian!), small pliars (thanks Mike!), canned air (thanks Susan!) and paper towels.

problem: . Oven intermittently would not heat and turntable wouldn't turn. At repair event the probable issue was determined to be a series of switches that are engaged by the door. Went ahead and ordered a latch hook, PHOK-A137WRFZ, two switches QSW-MA131WRE0 and a switch/fuse combination FFS-BA021WRK0. I removed the latch hook assembly and tested the three switches. They seemed fine. Installed the new latch hook with the new switches, but noticed that this assembly is designed to be adjustable and has "play" while the two screws that hold it aren't tightened. With the door closed, this assembly can be accurately aligned to optimally engage the switches. I did this and then tightened the two screws holding it with the hope they would not move over many years. The system works now without any intermittent failures. When the oven was in a state where it wouldn't start, it could reliably be started after going through one or more cycles of pushing the "open" mechanical button on the front while holding the door closed. This process is referred to in the service manual as helpful in aligning the latch hook. It also exercises the process of engaging the 3 switches on the latch hook and might guide people to this resolution.

problem: . The helpers showed me how to take off the bottom of the toaster (no screws). They commented that it was not meant to be repaired, which is why it was so difficult. Next they checked the electrical connections with a probe. Lastly, they bent some of the plastic pieces. That solved the problem so it stayed down and then popped up. If you don't have the equipment mentioned, come to a Fixit Clinic. First, unscrew the bottom. If there are no screws, look for the only thing that can be what is holding the bottom of the toaster on. Using a pair of pliers, turn the metal parts sticking up 90 degrees. It took me several tries to get a good grip. If you have a tool that detects a circuit, then put one probe on a ground (I think) and the other end on the connections in the thing that makes the toaster pop up. Test each connection succesively (there were several in my toaster). If the connections are sound. then look at the plastic pieces and try to determine where they are preventing the toaster from staying down. Very carefully, bend them, but not so far that they break. Good luck.

problem: The item was completely fixed at the repair event. The fan had stopped working. First the fuse in the cord was checked. Then the facing of the fan had to be removed and the problem was diagnosed as the thermal fuse in the motor compartment. problem: . We fixed it! We ordered the replacement part the same day, got it the next day, and it worked! Before the fixit clinic, the only thing I could possibly test was whether the thermostat was still working by trying to click it on. But considering that it didn’t seem to power on at all, that test wasn’t very conclusive. Our problem ended up being electrical; the overload protector was broken. We had a multimeter on hand and with our fixit helpers, we stepped through testing every component via a helpful schematic provided on the back of the fridge and concluded it must be the overload protector. We tested this by removing the part and directly connecting the power to the compressor. It turned on and started humming! Thankfully the problem wasn’t the compressor and the new part was only $8 to try. My recommendation would be to have a multimeter on hand to test the electrical components. YouTube mentioned that most problems with mini fridges tended to be electrical and we were happy to find that it was. I was concerned that the compressor was broken, which would likely be a much more expensive and involved repair.

problem:
C'est un four micro onde qui possède également la fonction chaleur tournante. Ce four à la particularité de posséder un clapet amovible situé dans la cavité qui contient la lampe d'éclairage du four, cavité qui est attenante à la chambre de chauffe et qui communique avec celle-ci à travers une grille. Je ne sais pas à quoi sert ce clapet : évacuation de la chaleur ou de l'humidité ? Dans la fonction micro onde ou dans la fonction chaleur tournante ? Je ne sais pas. 

Depuis quelques semaines, le four s'éteint spontanément après une minute exactement, qu'il soit utilisé en fonction micro onde ou en fonction chaleur tournante. Après avoir cherché sur internet, je suis tombé sur quelques article mentionnant que le clapet pouvait être la source du problème. J'ai effectivement remarqué dans un premier temps que le clapet s'ouvrait et se fermait en cours de chauffe (et dans les deux types de fonctions) de façon apparemment erratique. 

J'ai ensuite ouvert le four pour faire quelques tests. Le clapet est surmonté par un moteur rotatif qui le commande, et ce clapet bute sur un détecteur lorsqu'il est dans sa position fermée. 
* En démarrant en mode chaleur tournante, le moteur tourne dans le sens anti-horlogique si la position du clapet au départ est fermée. Si la position de départ est ouvert, alors le moteur tourne dans un des deux sens de manière apparemment aléatoire. Le four s'arrête au bout d'une minute. 
* Si pendant la première minute je ferme le clapet (ou l'ouvre puis le ferme), Alors le moteur s'arrête et le four continue au delà de la minute. 
* En démarrant en mode micro ondes, le moteur tourne dans le sens anti-horlogique si la position du clapet au départ est ouverte. Si la position de départ est fermée, alors le moteur tourne dans un des deux sens de manière apparemment aléatoire. Le four s'arrête au bout d'une minute. 
* Si pendant la première minute je ferme le clapet en partant de la position ouverte, Alors le moteur s'arrête et le four continue au delà de la minute. J'ai le même comportement si je démarre avec le clapet position fermée et que je l'ouvre pendant la première minute. 

Merci d'avance pour votre aide.

problem:
Ik kocht deze versterker tweedehands in 2015. Het toestel is in goede algemene staat en het werkte perfect tot voor enkele weken. De klank viel bijna volledig weg, de lampjes van de infinium module gingen aan het branden en de powerled ging aan het knipperen. Dat wijst dan normaal gezien op een versleten eindversterkerlamp. Ik verving de beide eindversterkerlampen EL84-type door matched pair lampen van JJ electronics en ook de drie voorversterkerlampen 12AX7-type door Sovtek lampen. Als ik hem nu aanschakel geeft hij enkele seconden lang een normaal volume, maar valt dan terug op een lager volume.. Dat is wel redelijk, maar het geluid wordt bij het hoger instellen van het volume heel snel 'blurry'. De infinium module blijft dan aangeven dat één van beide lampen niet in orde zou zijn en de powerled knippert dan de hele tijd. 

Ik contacteerde al een amp-service, maar krijg geen reactie. Dan maar zélf aan de slag ermee? Het probleem is dat ik niet veel kaas heb gegeten van elektronica. Dus repairdershulp is meer dan welkom!
De versterker is het mij zeker waard om er wat moeite in te steken en eventueel ook materiaal aan te kopen om hem te herstellen. De cleane klank is voor een versterker uit deze prijsklasse - bijzonder goed. Ik maakte er enkele jaren geleden opnamen mee in een studio.

Het serienummer is: S1400702B03

problem:
Na het aansluiten van de meegeleverde voeding moest men vroeger op de power-knop duwen om het toestel aan te zetten, en nogmaals duwen om het weer af te zetten. De power-knop is geen mechanische aan-uit-knop, maar een eenvoudig drukknopje.

Tegenwoordig is het echter zo bij het aansluiten van de voeding het toestel meteen aanstaat (en dus niet manueel moet aangezet worden) en gewoon werkt, maar na het duwen op de power-knop om uit te zetten gebeurt er iets vreemds: enkel de ingebouwde eindversterker gaat uit (dat hoor je aan een relais dat intern klikt en de luidsprekers die geen lichte ruis meer te horen geven), maar al de rest blijft wel actief. Je kan alles schijnbaar blijven gebruiken, maar er komt geen geluid meer uit. Vanaf dan haalt drukken op de power-knop ook niets meer uit, de enige manier is de stekker uittrekken en herbeginnen. Ook een factory reset van het toestel loste niets op.

We hebben gedurende een tijdje overspanning gehad in onze wijk (250V en meer) en dan weer onderspanning (190V), en het is sinds toen dat het probleem zich voordoet.

Ik heb de service manual van het toestel, met o.a. alle elektrische en elektronische circuits.
